maximum_permitted_stay: Single-entry visitor eVisa: up to 3 months; cumulative maximum 3 months in any 12-month period.
passport_validity_rule: At least six months remaining on the passport at the point of entry.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count is published in the reviewed official eVisa guidance.
return_ticket_rule: The reviewed AIG FAQ does not state a universal return-ticket rule. An onward itinerary is a supporting document for landside transit up to 48 hours and for visitor stays of 48 hours or more.
proof_of_funds_rule: No fixed minimum funds amount or mandatory bank-statement requirement is published in the reviewed AIG visitor eVisa FAQ. AIG may request additional supporting evidence.
accommodation_rule: Accommodation information is requested as supporting information for stays of 48 hours or more; it is not listed as a universal mandatory document for every visitor application.
travel_insurance_rule: Medical/travel insurance is mandatory for the full stay and must cover all medical treatment and emergency air evacuation. Minimum air-evacuation cover is GBP 500,000; GBP 1 million overall cover is advised. Evidence is requested during application and at entry. Pre-existing conditions must be covered and declared.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Applicants must declare listed contagious diseases if currently suffering from them or if suffered within the preceding 12 months. Yellow fever is on the declaration list; the reviewed FAQ does not state a universal vaccination-certificate requirement.
transit_rule: A transit eVisa allows up to 7 days per journey; double transit permits a return stopover within 3 months. AIG may require a multiple-entry UK visa for UK visa nationals, valid for both outward and return journeys. Bangladesh is on the UK Home Office visa-national list, so this condition may apply and should be confirmed with AIG. Air access is via South Africa and St Helena; check South African transit/entry rules separately.
application_channel: Apply directly online through the Ascension Island Government eVisa portal; no third-party agents. One application per person; upload photo and insurance; pay by card or bank transfer. Apply at least 14 days before arrival.
application_fee: Visitor eVisa: GBP 40 standard; GBP 60 fast-track/priority; under-12s GBP 10. Non-refundable.
processing_time: AIG targets 90% of decisions within 21 days and all within 6 weeks; fast-track target is 14 days. These are targets, not guarantees.
required_documents: Valid ordinary Bangladesh passport with at least six months remaining; completed online visitor eVisa application; scanned JPEG photograph clearly showing the applicant's face; medical/travel insurance covering the full stay, medical treatment and emergency air evacuation (minimum GBP 500,000 evacuation cover); evidence of insurance. Additional documents may be requested by AIG.

review_notes: Bangladesh is not listed among the nationalities currently excluded from Ascension Island eVisa issuance. The AIG FAQ states that all nationalities require an eVisa except specified exempt classes; Bangladesh ordinary-passport tourists therefore use the visitor eVisa route. Bangladesh is on the UK Home Office visa-national list. AIG states that nationals who require a UK visa may be required to show a multiple-entry UK visa valid for both outward and return journeys before an Ascension eVisa is issued. This is worded as a possible, case-dependent condition, not an automatic requirement; applicants should obtain confirmation from AIG before travel. No visa-on-arrival facility exists. The AIG government immigration page returned HTTP 502 during this check; the accessible AIG eVisa portal FAQ and eligibility page are the primary evidence used.
